neighbours.label: the end of a narrative subject noun phrase, or the adverb right after it, just before its past-tense main verb of consequence (the post quickly (went), the stance quickly (prompted), the man in the blue coat (led))
fire: Within a day, the video quickly spread across social media.
That autumn, the new policy quickly sparked protests in the capital.
During the match, the young striker in the red boots scored twice.
Last spring the mayor's decision quickly drew criticism from the unions.
On the first night, the old woman with the lantern led us to the inn.
Soon after its release, the song quickly climbed to the top of the charts.
By noon the rumour quickly reached every office in the building.
In 1970 the small shop on the corner closed its doors for good.
quiet: Everyone watched the video on their phones in the evening.
That autumn, people read about the new policy in the papers.
During the match, fans cheered for the young striker in the red boots.
Last spring the unions wrote to the mayor about the decision.
On the first night, we met the old woman with the lantern at the inn.
Soon after its release, I heard the song on the radio.
By noon we had heard the rumour from several people.
In 1970 my parents bought bread at the small shop on the corner.
